title: Generalized Star Height at Most Three
main_claim: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has generalized star height at most 3 (complement taken in Σ*). Outline: fibers of a morphism T:Σ*→M are expressed using a prefix code E of episodes. There are two applications of a split identity. The inner split on an exceptional sublanguage D is decoded through a stencil and gives height 2. The outer split on E uses a robust tag clock, an end guard and a shift table, and gives height 3. Boolean affine recovery is applied after each split, and a remainder language of height ≤1 is concatenated at the end.

issues.description: The stated bound of 20 anchors is loose: the argument actually gives at most 7 markers plus 1 mismatch, so 8. Only the budget constant changes, and in the safe direction.
issues.evidence: Interval length < (31/5)d_• with marker separation d_• gives ≤7 markers, plus the shared q_0.

issues.description: The template compilation proof is a sketch. It claims every bounded-offset datum (marker searches near the start or end, crossing products, φ of end-relative anchors mod n, periodic agreement) is ultimately periodic in i on a c^i b. That is correct, but the stabilization threshold is only asserted, not made explicit. I do not consider this a mathematical gap.
issues.evidence: 'Choose a threshold and a common period beyond which their whole array is periodic.'

coverage:
I read all 10 sections in full. Checks made:
- Shift-table lemma: LLL dependency count, conditional independence of lines, and the quantifier order.
- Split identity: alignment induction and the height bound max{2,1+H}.
- Affine recovery and the homogeneous lift.
- Robust clock: the left/right partition probability bound (m^4(15/16)^{a0}<1); compatibility via first coordinates; reversal exclusion via Type1/Type2 differences (1/24 vs 2/100); the C_I+C_J center sums (all of Z/6, checked); diagonal margins; forest-coordinate counting a0+4F^2 b0 < 10^7 log 2m.
- Marker lemma: radius and overlap arguments.
- Stencil residues r_i = 4N^2 i + i^2 mod B: distinctness checked.
- Periodic-cut lemma: lag inequalities, constancy of c^{|M|+aN_MB}, and that gcd(d'N_MB, n)=1 so the full image is swept.
- Shared end guard, in both the marker and mismatch cases.
- Outer split soundness for off-diagonal, equal-main and equal-periodic pairs, including the residue u being forced by B | k−t; completeness via the ball/net hit and ¬Z, ¬A_*.
- Sparsity count: end instability ≤4; clock ≤ c log(2m) per anchor; inner markers ≤3 per (Q,j); total budget < μ.
- Decoder: the true witness survives in both branches, uniqueness, and the final end check.
- Inner split: total table ψ_e over all of M, and kinds covering all ψ.
- Compilation and the remainder language.
No sibling reports were present for family 134.
